posts.title: Closing summary
posts.text: We’re wrapping up this live coverage of the US ground stop and travel chaos that followed – it’s just passed 12.50am in Washington DC. Below’s a rundown on what happened, and you can read a full report here. Thanks for being with us. The Federal Aviation Administration declared a nationwide ground stop on Friday…

posts.title: US airport chaos continues – in pictures
posts.text: Here are some of the latest images coming in from US airports as the disruption from the FAA’s nationwide ground stop continues while some airlines slowly start resuming flights.

Just to recap, travel plans were thrown into chaos across the US on Friday afternoon as passengers on planes and in airport terminals were suddenly thrust into limbo due to the nationwide ground stop. Even now that the stoppage has been lifted, airlines will not be able to return to normal operations immediately…

Delta has also said it is restarting flights, posting on social media: The FAA-mandated ground stop has been lifted and we are safely resuming flights. Thank you for your understanding as we work as quickly as possible to fully restore normal operations. Southwest Airlines said it was resuming a limited number of…

posts.title: Airlines start resuming flights after ban lifted
posts.text: US airlines have slowly begun resuming flights on Friday night after the FAA-mandated ground stop was lifted. United Airlines said it was resuming operations, “including some Friday night flights”. “Safety is our highest priority as we take care of our customers and employees,” the airline said in a post to X.

American Airlines says it will operate as many flights as possible on Friday night and aim for a strong recovery from the disruption. The airline posted on social media: The FAA’s nationwide ground stop has been lifted. We’re focused on operating as many remaining flights as possible this evening while positioning the…

All US-bound departures from European airports are suspended until 5am UTC on Saturday, according to a notice published by the European traffic control agency, Eurocontrol. Forty-two European countries are members of Eurocontrol, including the 27 EU countries, the UK, Turkey and Israel. The notice, issued by Network…

Ben Doherty, a Guardian Australia reporter, is currently on a plane at Sydney airport, waiting to fly to the US. He writes: US-bound flights out of Sydney in Australia have been held on the tarmac, some for up to three hours. Flights are being gradually cleared for departure after being held in Australia by the FAA…

posts.title: What we know so far about the US flight fiasco that's grounded thousands of planes nationwide
posts.text: If you’re just joining us, we’re continuing our live coverage of the major systems failure that led US aviation officials to ground flights nationwide for more than four hours on Friday. That continues to cause chaos for thousands of air travelers across the US and the world. Here is what we know about the rare…

posts.title: Follow our continuing coverage
posts.text: This blog is closing, but the Guardian is continuing our live coverage of the US flight fiasco in this newly launched live blog.

posts.title: Ground stop lifts, but airport chaos and questions over US aviation system failure remain
posts.text: While the US Federal ⁠Aviation Administration has now lifted the nationwide ground stop imposed on airports just before 4pm Eastern Time, the question of what caused the communications outage that paralyzed the air-traffic control system remains to be answered. On social media, Democrats on the House homeland security…

posts.title: White House briefing filled with praise for Trump ends without clear explanation of what went wrong
posts.text: Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, and Markwayne Mullin, the head of homeland security, just concluded their briefing on the hours-long communications outage that led to chaos at US airports on Friday. Both men peppered their remarks with lavish praise for Donald Trump, who was curiously quiet during the…

posts.title: Mullin appears to suggest older technology used by FAA was overwhelmed with data from new equipment
posts.text: Briefing reporters at the White House on Friday, Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, and Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, used the nationwide outage to press for more funding to overhaul the nation’s air-traffic-control system. Both secretaries appeared to suggest that the cause of Friday’s…

posts.title: 'We have seen zero evidence that this was this was a cyber-attack,' Mullin says
posts.text: Markwayne Mullin, the US homeland security secretary, just told reporters at a briefing on the FAA outage that brought US aviation to a standpoint, “we’ve seen zero evidence that this was a cyber-attack.” “Now, when we start looking at cyber threats, cyber-attacks, typically some people are going to raise their hand…

posts.title: Duffy says airspace is open, 'but it's going to take us some time to unwind what's happened'
posts.text: Speaking in the White House briefing room, Sean Duffy, the former Fox News host now serving as US transportation secretary, just said that the federal government has “identified the problem” that brought down the US air traffic control system on Friday and the system “is operational right now”. “So at 8.15 tonight,…

posts.title: FAA lifts ground stop re-opening US airports
posts.text: The nationwide ground stop on departures from US airports has been lifted, the US Federal ⁠Aviation Administration said in an advisory on its website Friday. Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary is now speaking at a press briefing in the White House, and began by praising Donald Trump, but did not immediately…

posts.title: 'This is what the leadership of President Trump looks like,' Markwayne Mullin says
posts.text: “This is what the leadership of President Trump looks like,” Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary just said at the start of a briefing on the crisis at US airports.

Ronald Reagan Washington National is no longer accepting diverted aircraft, the FAA says. Earlier on Friday, at least 600 flights were diverted during the nationwide groundstop, to airports including Reagan Washington, Chicago O’Hare, Denver international, and Dallas Fort Worth international.

posts.title: Trump tells Fox News FAA outage does not seem like a cyber-attack since 'there’s nobody taking credit'
posts.text: While Donald Trump has spent hours out of sight during the crisis that paralyzed America’s airports on Friday, Fox News reports that the president told its White House correspondent, Peter Doocy, that the vast telecommunications outage does not seem like a cyber-attack. “I did just talk to President Trump on the…

posts.title: US transportation secretary Sean Duffy due to brief public soon, White House says
posts.text: We are standing by for the start of a briefing, the first of the day, from the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, on the crisis that halted all departures from US airports for hours on Friday. Once the briefing begins, we will bring you updates.

Democrats have filled the vacuum, demanding answers. Congresswoman Nellie Pou, a New…

posts.text: New Orleans mayor Helena Moreno said all passengers and crew have been accounted for in what she called “truly a miracle on the Mississippi.” She added the ship narrowly missed striking a bridge carrying around 160,000 vehicles daily. Thirty-two people are now being treated at a local hospital. Those include two New…

Devon Flanagan was at his job nearby at the Port of New Orleans when workers began rushing down the dock. He got out of his truck and noticed the American Heritage on its side and passengers in the water. “It was…

posts.title: What we know so far
posts.text: A tanker collided with a river cruise liner, the American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage, carrying 129 passengers plus crew in New Orleans on Friday. The cruise liner was taking on water as it rapidly turned on its side, and videos showed people climbing on to the railing to avoid falling in the water. New Orleans…

Congressman Troy Carter, the representative for Louisiana’s 2nd congressional district, said in a statement that he was devastated by news of the crash. “I am monitoring the situation closely and praying for the swift rescue of survivors and for all emergency crews responding to the situation,” he wrote on social…

A video circulating around social media shows a different angle during the moment the ship was falling on its side into the water. Passengers can be seen climbing onto the balconies’ railing to avoid sliding into the river as the ship turned horizontally. Several uniformed people can be seen running away from the…

Martin J Davies, a maritime expert at Tulane University, told local news outlet Fox 8 that he suspected the incident was caused by either steerage failure or engine failure. “This ship is headed upriver and for it to have lost the ability to avoid the moored vessel, there must have been some fairly substantial…

posts.title: Photos show ongoing rescue efforts at the site of the crash
posts.text: Pictures are now coming in from the news wires. Emergency personnel and crews can be seen on the scene after a tanker crashed into a river cruise in New Orleans. The cruise liner can be seen lying on its side:

posts.title: Officials to hold news conference at 3pm CST
posts.text: Officials said they will be holding a news conference at 3pm CST, to begin in about ten minutes, providing further updates on the collision. We will bring you those latest updates as they come. A statement from the US coast guard also announced that the river “is closed to all vessel traffic between mile markers 93…

The New Orleans Regional Transit Authority said in a statement on social media that ferry service across the Mississippi River has been temporarily suspended as a precaution following the collision. Travelers are encouraged to seek alternate routes.

posts.title: Multiple people rescued from river, says New Orleans mayor
posts.text: New Orleans mayor Helena Moreno’s communication team said multiple individuals have been rescued, and search-and-rescue operations remain ongoing, according to a local Fox News affiliate.

Some US cities have reported their Microsoft services are now returning after the global outage. The sheriff’s office in Arapahoe County, Colorado, which previously reported the outage was affecting online bond payments, said the issue has been resolved.
